reviewType: independent AI editorial review; not human approval
sourceSentence: Old songs remain part of the city's cultural memory.

owner406Comparison.verdict: Defensibly distinct, with an explicit detector-scope note required.
owner406Comparison.owner406: Owner 406 teaches the longer verb phrase 'uncover a layer of cultural memory': discovering a particular aspect of a remembered past from evidence, without making it the whole history. Its source is family letters being read as an uncovering experience.
owner406Comparison.proposed2646: This draft teaches the standalone noun phrase 'cultural memory': whether an already remembered song, practice, place or story belongs to a community's shared memory. The source states continuing membership in the city's memory, not a new discovery. The lesson's strongest distinct choices are private versus communal memory, vanished building versus remembered practice, and documentation versus endorsement.
owner406Comparison.overlapLimit: Both lessons necessarily explain shared remembrance and variation among accounts. The proposed target regex also matches 'cultural memory' inside owner 406's complete source phrase. Module-specific rendering may still keep lessons separate, but do not use a bare regex hit to declare the 406 source owned by 2646. Record this nested-construction exception or constrain the detector before selection.

findings.issue: English says families still 'explain it to newcomers'; Traditional Chinese says they explain '其由來' (its origin). That adds an origin claim absent from English and salient because the lesson elsewhere says origin accounts may differ.
findings.recommendedFix: Use '家庭仍向新來者解說這項活動' or another Chinese line about explaining the seed exchange itself, without asserting they explain its origin. The English audio can remain unchanged.

findings.issue: The prompt says elders teach younger people to make a traditional kite frame. The model changes this to 'fold the traditional frame' / '摺出傳統框架', an unprovided method that sounds questionable for a kite frame, which is usually assembled or bent rather than folded.
findings.recommendedFix: Use 'make' or 'assemble the traditional kite frame' and matching Chinese, preserving the named annual workshop, different origin accounts and target phrase. Revalidate all example-derived glossary spans after editing.

findings.issue: The bare /cultural memory/ detector matches all four proposed source sentences, but also matches the phrase inside owner 406's full 'uncover a layer of cultural memory' source and keyed lines. The lessons can remain distinct by construction and learner decision, yet a cross-owner detector screen will show a collision.
findings.recommendedFix: Document an intentional nested-expression exception keyed to the complete owner 406 construction, or add a bounded guard excluding 'a layer of cultural memory' while retaining all four proposed full-source matches and this draft's keyed forms. Test both owners' source sentences and inflected 406 forms before integration.

findings.issue: Several wrong options use near-absolute impossibilities ('every retired worker ... exactly the same way', a demolished building means no shared memory can remain, every resident used it identically). The keys are unambiguous, but students can discard some foils without deciding what cultural memory means.
findings.recommendedFix: Replace one or two with plausible near-misses drawn from the stated evidence, such as treating the workshop as merely a technical lesson without its shared port history, or mistaking differing accounts for proof that no common practice existed. Keep exactly one best key and align each Chinese option.

findings.issue: Most affirmative assessments involve active annual teaching or retelling, while the source only says old songs remain part of a city's cultural memory. The brief itself allows stories, practices or places; active instruction to newcomers should be an example, not a requirement for membership in cultural memory.
findings.recommendedFix: Include or discuss one supported case of shared remembered material that persists through recognition, archives or community recollection without requiring a currently repeated workshop. Retain the private-versus-communal boundary and avoid claiming mere archival existence proves broad public remembrance.

checklist.evidence: All four source IDs, book/question/sample/page locators and exact repeated sentence match the source inventory. The draft does not infer a sports or products scenario from the repeated sentence.

Standalone shared-memory noun versus discovery of one layer is a useful construction and decision difference. Shared remembrance/variation overlap is acknowledged; nested detector needs explicit handling (R2646-03).

checklist.gate: Seven steps, six questions, four audio roles
checklist.evidence: Focused build and --check produced 1 lesson, 6 questions, 4 audio requests and 0 review flags. No audio was synthesized or listened to.

checklist.gate: Six keyed questions and single-best standard answers
checklist.evidence: Listening a, scene a, contrast a and dialogue a are each uniquely supported; the reply golden b is natural and target-bearing. Some standard distractors are remote or absolute (R2646-04).
All a–d offer a cautious, usable exhibition-label approach that names continuing practice or preserves multiple family accounts; only golden b contains the target phrase.

The stages cover intergenerational practice, careful attribution, memory after a building disappears, private versus shared recollection, recording a harmful rule without endorsement, a spoken village example and changed-context exhibit writing. Variation among accounts recurs, but the decisions are not identical.

The noun phrase is natural and the shared-memory sense is preserved. Model 2's 'fold the traditional frame' is an unsupported and likely awkward kite-making detail (R2646-02); positive cases overemphasize active teaching (R2646-05).
Most translations preserve actors, qualification, negation and uncertainty. Speaking Chinese adds an origin explanation absent from English (R2646-01).

Native-JS regex matches all four full source sentences and every target-bearing keyed model; speaking [50,65] slices exactly 'cultural memory'. It also matches inside owner 406's longer construction (R2646-03).
All six English glossary spans exactly equal contiguous substrings of their cited suggested answers. None contains cultural memory; recheck after any writing edit.

Harbour knots, market recipe, bathhouse, school rule, seeds, hill bell and kite frame differ from the guide's old-songs example. The final exhibit writing is a new context and provides two complete English/Chinese models.
